description_en: The pillar is located on the side of a narrow path, to the north of the old village of Mānmā.Stone pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 17th century. They are installed to honor the memory of deceased persons, mostly warriors (Andolfatto 2019).The pillar is oriented to the south, which is probably its original orientation. The southern side is decorated with carvings. On top is a star motif. The central register is occupied by the representation of a horse rider. To the right of the horse rider is another character. These probably represent a deceased warrior and his wife. Below are two of three lines of a very eroded inscription. Another star motif occupies the lower register. Exceptionally the two sides of the pillar are also carved, with triangular motifs and one star or flower pattern.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne University, 2019.
